review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Failure to restore the band despite confirmed tag expression would indicate the KO-sensitive band was an indirect effect
errors.issue: Failed rescue can instead reflect altered localization, processing, function or recognition of the construct. Expression alone does not exclude those alternatives.

errors.quote: Peptides identified in the 75-kDa region *assign* the unknown band
errors.issue: Co-migrating proteins and immunoprecipitated partners need to be distinguished from the directly recognized antigen.

errors.quote: Loss of the 50-kDa band is not an artifact of unequal protein loading or transfer
errors.issue: Comparable loading does not establish equivalent transfer of the particular species.

rationale: Good recognition of full coding deletion, unknown expected mass, indirect dependence and application specificity. A size-shifting rescue is useful, but negative outcomes and proteomic identities are overinterpreted, so the proposed resolution is less decisive than claimed.
reference_guardrails: Comparable loading does not establish antigen identity or guarantee equivalent transfer of each species.
No expected target molecular mass is supplied. Do not assume 50 kDa is the predicted full-length mass.
Untagged rescue may restore either the target or an indirectly dependent antigen.
Gel-slice proteomics and native immunoprecipitation can contain co-migrating proteins or partners; identity of a constituent is not automatically identity of the immunoreactive species.
No requirement to mention private draft status or obsolete multiple-choice distractors.
Complete coding deletion blocks new target synthesis; pre-existing protein and signal mixtures are possible caveats when timing and turnover are unspecified, not established explanations.
A reference list of methods does not make any single validation approach infallible.
